Consider two primitive polynomials f(x) and g(x) in a UFD R[x]. We want to show that their product f(x)g(x) is also primitive.

Let p(x) be the least common multiple of the denominators of the leading coefficients of f(x) and g(x). Since f(x) and g(x) are primitive, their leading coefficients are relatively prime to p(x). Therefore, there exist polynomials a(x) and b(x) in R[x] such that a(x)p(x) + b(x)p(x) = 1.

Now, consider the product f(x)g(x). Let c(x) be the leading coefficient of f(x)g(x). Then c(x) = c1(x)c2(x), where c1(x) and c2(x) are the leading coefficients of f(x) and g(x), respectively.

Since a(x)p(x) + b(x)p(x) = 1, we have a(x)c1(x) + b(x)c2(x) = 1. Therefore, the leading coefficient of f(x)g(x) is coprime to p(x).

Since p(x) is the least common multiple of the denominators of the leading coefficients of f(x) and g(x), we have that p(x) divides the denominator of the leading coefficient of f(x)g(x). Therefore, the leading coefficient of f(x)g(x) is a unit in R[x].

Hence, the product f(x)g(x) is primitive.

Now, suppose that f(x) and g(x) are coprime in R[x]. We want to show that they are coprime in F[x], the field of fractions.

Let p(x) be the least common multiple of the denominators of the leading coefficients of f(x) and g(x). Since f(x) and g(x) are coprime in R[x], we have that p(x) divides the denominator of the leading coefficient of f(x) or the denominator of the leading coefficient of g(x).

Therefore, the leading coefficient of f(x)g(x) is a unit in F[x], since it is a multiple of p(x).

Hence, f(x) and g(x) are coprime in F[x].

Therefore, the product of two primitive polynomials in a UFD R[x] is primitive, and if f and g are coprime in R[x], they are coprime in F[x].
